clue.text: No longer in custody, but not conforming

definitions.meaning: freed from being kept under guard, released from detention

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both literally, as released from someone's custody, and idiomatically, as incongruous or inappropriate.

clue.text: One who must go on working with a stroke

definitions.text: One who must go on working with a stroke

parts.words: One who must go on working with a stroke
parts.note: reads like an invalid struggling on after an illness, but the stroke is a pull on a rowing blade

explanation.surface: Someone carries on with their job despite suffering a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower works by repeated strokes of the oar, and the stroke is also the crew member setting the pace.

clue.text: Skinnier, but solvent

definitions.meaning: a liquid used to dilute paint

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of thin means skinnier, and paint thinner is a solvent used to dilute paint.

clue.text: Display of lilies, say, at bottom of river

parts.note: a crossword joke: a river is something that flows, a flow-er
a bed is the bottom of a river or the sea

explanation.surface: Lilies are growing at the bottom of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom of river' is a riverbed; read with the river as a FLOWER (something that flows), the bed of it gives the garden feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plot planted with lilies or other blooms makes a colourful show, an example of the defined display.

clue.text: Dread losing time for fault

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word for dread

parts.note: dread means terror

explanation.surface: Someone's fear fades as time goes by, mistaken for a flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault and a mistake are synonyms, as in a fault in the accounts.

clue.text: 19 dn drops article supporting river authority

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

indicators.note: drops tells us the article is removed from the other answer

parts.note: the answer to 19 down, a temporary occupation
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tenancy loses an item while backing a river authority.
explanation.walkthrough: TENANCY (19 down) 'drops' AN to leave TENCY, which goes under PO because 'supporting' in a down clue means below.
explanation.definitionFit: Potency is power or force, and authority likewise means the power to command or influence.

clue.text: Crackpot finds teachers patient

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
a doctor's patient is a case

explanation.surface: An eccentric discovers that the teaching staff are tolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like an adjective (tolerant) but is the noun: a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot and a nutcase are both informal words for a crazy or eccentric person.

clue.text: Flashing advert needed to move motor cars even cars

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Flashing advert needed to move motor cars even cars (8,4)' is garbled: SPARKING + PLUG accounts for 'Flashing advert', but 'even cars' has no job and the scan is blank, so the true wording is unknown

clue.text: Split, for example, one firm with a covered walkway

parts.note: Split is a port city on the Croatian coast
the Roman numeral I is one
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A Croatian town and a business have a roofed promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a verb or a break; with its capital it is the Croatian port.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a roofed porch or colonnade, a walkway covered by a roof on columns.

clue.text: Sharp rap for Mongol holding army back

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembled piece is read in the reverse direction
holding means one word contains the other

parts.note: the Tatars were a people of the Mongol hordes
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A Mongol warrior keeps his army in reserve for a sudden knock.
explanation.walkthrough: TATAR 'holding' TA gives TATATAR, and 'back' turns it all round.
explanation.definitionFit: This imitative word describes a quick series of knocks, such as a sharp rap on a door.

clue.text: Fiddle the merry-go-round receipts?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, the takings from giving people a ride at the fair

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deceive or cheat, and literally it describes money taken for a fairground ride.

clue.text: Love affair recollected in Cremona

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected, gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A love affair is remembered in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' means remembered on the surface, but as 're-collected' it signals rearranging the letters of CREMONA, an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, a relationship of courtship and passion.

clue.text: Line of soldiers holding bag for loot

indicators.note: holding means the word for a line encloses another

parts.note: a rank is a line of soldiers standing side by side
a sac is a bag-like part of an animal or plant

explanation.surface: Troops in formation carry a sack of plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To loot a place is to plunder it, the same as to ransack it.

clue.text: Not the first offender, this sort of man

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the word for offender is removed

parts.note: an offender against moral law is a sinner

explanation.surface: Someone is not the original culprit, but a man of a certain kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the phrase 'the inner man', meaning one's spiritual self or one's appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom 'the inner man', the inner self or soul, this adjective describes the kind of man meant.

clue.text: Contents of tin that made Hector complain

parts.note: to hector is to bully
to beef is slang for to complain

explanation.surface: What was in a can made the Trojan hero Hector grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H suggests Homer's Trojan hero, but 'Hector' is the verb meaning to bully. BULLY BEEF is tinned corned beef, a British army staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Bully beef is corned beef, typically sold and eaten from a tin.

clue.text: Glasses that have to be held up for inspection

definitions.text: Glasses that have to be held up for inspection

parts.words: Glasses that have to be held up for inspection
parts.note: spectacles with no arms that are raised on a handle to the eyes when looking at something

explanation.surface: Some glasses must be raised to be examined.
explanation.definitionFit: These spectacles have a long handle and are held up to the eyes rather than worn.

clue.text: It goes up and down like a barrage balloon

definitions.text: It goes up and down like a barrage balloon

parts.words: It goes up and down like a barrage balloon
parts.note: a large structure that rises and sinks as it fills and empties of fuel stored inside

explanation.surface: Something bobs up and down like a wartime barrage balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer's telescopic tank rises when full of town gas and falls when emptied, as a balloon does.

clue.text: Top commander may mix up Morse

indicators.note: to mix something up is to jumble it into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A senior officer might confuse Morse code signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix up' reads as a phrase, but 'mix' is the anagram signal and 'up' is part of the fodder with MORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is a person in overall charge, such as a supreme military commander.

clue.text: Extra weapon for this sort of bowler

parts.note: over means extra or surplus, as in left over
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler gets an extra weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an overarm bowler delivers with the arm brought over the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bowling is done overarm, with the arm swung above the shoulder, so the answer describes such a bowler.

clue.text: Wind down from record run

parts.note: to record something is to tape it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A breeze dies down after a record run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as moving air, but 'Wind down' is a verb phrase: to diminish gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to diminish gradually, to wind down or tail off.

clue.text: Note on girl's temporary occupation

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A note is left on a girl's short-term lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the holding of a property as a tenant, for a limited period, so a temporary occupation.

clue.text: Governor's wise course

parts.note: governor is old slang for father, so Pa's
sage means wise

explanation.surface: A ruler adopts a prudent policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Governor' suggests an official, but it is informal British slang for one's father, giving PA'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a course or way through, as in a passage through the mountains.

clue.text: To do this the deaf may encounter studied insolence at first

definitions.text: To do this the deaf may

indicators.note: at first places the word for insolence at the start

parts.note: lip is slang for insolence, cheek
to have read a subject is to have studied it

explanation.surface: Deaf people may meet deliberate rudeness at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'studied insolence' reads as calculated rudeness, but splits into READ (studied) and LIP (insolence), with 'at first' putting LIP in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading lets deaf people follow speech by watching the speaker's mouth movements.

clue.text: Settle wife in Dingley area

indicators.note: in means the wife's letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: Dingley Dell is a place in Dickens's Pickwick Papers; a dell is a small wooded hollow

explanation.surface: A man settles his wife in a country spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dingley Dell, from Dickens's Pickwick Papers, lets 'Dingley area' stand for DELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle somewhere is to make one's home there, which is to dwell.

clue.text: Failure to exercise right no nurse can afford

indicators.note: can afford read as can provide, the letters of no nurse can give up a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: No nurse can afford to give up a right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can afford' is a loose anagram signal: the letters of NO NURSE can afford (yield) the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, non-user is the failure to use a right, which can cause the right to lapse.

clue.text: Handy bomb in position to entrap opponents

indicators.note: to entrap is to hold inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: a grade is a position or rank
E and N, East and North, are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A bomb is placed in position to snare enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so E and N are opponents. A 'handy bomb' is one thrown by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, hence handy.

clue.text: Brown, possibly dark, mug

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of dark could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A brown, perhaps dark, drinking vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' with a capital looks like a name; it is the colour TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, usually for beer.

clue.text: Creatures preserved here in accordance with rules of a French park

parts.note: formal means following set conventions or rules
de is French for of
Hyde Park is the famous royal park in central London

explanation.surface: Animals are kept in a properly run Parisian park.
explanation.walkthrough: HYDE Park is a large park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Biological specimens are traditionally kept in jars of this preserving solution.
